des_teaser.label: Teaser hero image — empty stage with single microphone

content.prompt: Editorial illustration: a dark theatrical comedy-club stage seen from the back of a mostly-empty house, stage lights casting a warm amber pool onto a single standing microphone on a rug. A faint glow of warm stage smoke. Moody, cinematic, 35mm photographic look, low-key lighting, deep blacks, no people, no text, no logos. Muted palette: deep charcoal, warm amber, wine red accent. Aspect ratio landscape 16:9.

des_teaser.brief: Full-viewport hero image before the headline. Warm amber mic on a dark stage, no people visible. Serves as atmospheric entry point — the quiet before a comedy special begins, inviting the reader into the room.
des_teaser.rationale: A generated image was chosen over a video so the hero loads instantly and sets a theatrical mood. No text or faces keep it evergreen and avoid likeness concerns.

des_01_overlay.label: Hook — 46-minute callback arc overlay

content.initial_state: A thin horizontal timeline spanning minute 0 to minute 59. Two dots are marked: the source line at 4:46 (small, muted amber) and the callback trigger at 50:57 (larger, warm red). A curved arc connects them, starting at 0% opacity.
content.transition: Over 1.5s, the arc fades in and then traces from the source point (4:46) to the trigger point (50:57). Small labels appear: 'mom / third-world country' at source, 'miscarriage joke' at trigger. A counter at the arc's midpoint counts from 0:00 to 46:11.
content.payoff: Reader sees the distance — nearly the full length of the show — that the callback spans before the body text starts, establishing the visual vocabulary for section 4.
content.style: dark editorial, thin amber curve on charcoal, labels in system-ui 13px, no axis ticks

des_01_overlay.brief: A minimalist animated arc that draws the distance between the source bit (4:46) and the callback payoff (50:57) on a slim timeline strip. This is the visual tag for the whole piece — the reader sees the 46-minute span before they have to believe it in words.
des_01_overlay.rationale: An animated arc concretely shows the scale of the gap in a way prose cannot. Chose this over a chart because the hook section needs a single striking image-moment, not a multi-series chart.

des_02_nesting.label: Nesting levels — zoomable topic tree / stacked bars

content.interaction: Hover tooltip shows count + percent of total segments. Clicking a bar dims the others.

des_02_nesting.brief: Horizontal bar chart of 6 nesting levels: level 1 (10 segments), 2 (21), 3 (43 — widest), 4 (31), 5 (19), 6 (7). The pyramidal shape IS the finding — it widens, then narrows, as you go deeper. Amber-to-rust gradient from level 1 (shallowest) to level 6 (deepest).
des_02_nesting.rationale: A bar chart makes the pyramidal shape immediately legible; hovering a bar surfaces the per-level count. Considered a treemap or sunburst but those make the counts harder to read.

des_02_callout.label: 85% stat callout — marriage + pregnancy dominate

content.label: of the hour is two macro-topics: marriage (30.7 min) + pregnancy (19.3 min)

des_02_callout.brief: Large 72px stat with a smaller label below. Placed inside section 2. Anchors the 'two-act structure' claim in one line.
des_02_callout.rationale: One striking number speaks for itself; a chart would dilute it.

des_03_timeline.label: Laughter timeline — 59 minutes, 2 peaks

content.interaction: Hover tooltip: 'min X: Y.Ys of laughter'.

style.palette: warm amber fill on dark background

des_03_timeline.brief: Area chart showing laugh-seconds per minute across all 59 minutes. Annotate the two peaks (minute 11 and minute 49) and the quiet minute 36. This is the visual centerpiece of section 3 — the jagged mountain range.
des_03_timeline.rationale: Area chart over line chart because the filled area conveys the cumulative 'amount of laughter' sensation better than a thin line. Annotations are critical because the chart's whole point is that two peaks are tied — without annotations the reader may miss which ones matter.

des_04_callbacks.label: Callback arcs — interactive source/trigger visualization

content.initial_state: A horizontal timeline strip (0 to 59 min) with three curved arcs above it connecting source points to trigger points: hippies (16:35 → 49:43), mom (4:46 → 50:57), wet (44:24 → 56:48). Arcs are semi-transparent amber curves. Each source and trigger is a small dot.
content.trigger: hover (desktop) or tap (mobile) on any arc
content.transition: On hover, the arc intensifies (opacity goes to 1, color shifts to warm red). A two-line caption appears below the strip: the exact source line and the payoff line from analyst.json ana_11. Other arcs dim to 0.3 opacity.
content.payoff: The reader can browse the three callbacks, see where they reach from/to, and read the exact words on both ends. Makes the structural argument tactile.
content.style: dark editorial, 360px tall, arcs in amber/rust, timeline in thin gray, source/trigger dots 8px, caption serif 16px

des_04_callbacks.brief: Interactive arc diagram visualizing all three callbacks on one timeline. Hovering an arc reveals the source and payoff quotes verbatim. This is the single most important visual in the piece — it is where the reader experiences the structural claim as a direct interaction.
des_04_callbacks.rationale: Interactive over static because the three callbacks each have a different story; static would overwhelm. Strongly preferred per editor's [MEDIA: interactive] hint and the section's role as the narrative turn.

des_04_conception.label: 38 laugh-s/min conception stat callout

content.label: laugh-seconds per minute during the 24-second conception bit — 3× the show's average

des_04_conception.brief: Large stat pulled from ana_13 to anchor the laugh-density finding. Sits below the callback arc interactive.
des_04_conception.rationale: The conception-bit density number is a key supporting fact and deserves standalone emphasis.

des_05_runway.label: Runway image — the callback as setup, not payoff

content.prompt: Editorial illustration: an airplane runway photographed at night from ground level, a long row of amber and blue runway lights stretching toward a dark horizon, wet asphalt reflecting the lights, atmospheric haze, cinematic low-key lighting, no people, no text, mood of suspended anticipation.

des_05_runway.brief: Atmospheric image anchoring the 'runway/plane' metaphor in section 5: a callback does not itself land the big laugh, it sets up the bit that does. Warm amber runway lights on a dark wet surface, stretching toward the horizon.
des_05_runway.rationale: A literal runway image supports the editorial metaphor without over-illustrating. Editor's [MEDIA: image] hint and the section's quieter, analytical tone call for a still image, not a chart or interactive.

des_06_depth_duration.label: Bit duration shrinks with depth — line/bar chart

content.interaction: Hover tooltip shows mean, median, and count at that level.

des_06_depth_duration.brief: Bar chart showing how average segment duration shrinks at deeper nesting levels: 471s → 156s → 82s → 57s → 47s → 30s. The 16x compression ratio is the takeaway — visualized here as a clean descent.
des_06_depth_duration.rationale: Bar chart chosen because the category (nesting level) is ordinal and the quantity (duration) varies by ~16x — a bar encoding makes the comparison legible. Log scale considered but rejected because the linear descent is itself part of the finding.

des_07_blueprint.label: Closing image — architectural blueprint as metaphor

content.prompt: Editorial illustration: an empty architectural blueprint on warm vellum paper, with nested rectangles drawn in red ink showing a hierarchical structure, a draftsman's triangle and compass resting on the edge, warm desk lamp lighting, no text readable, no numbers, cinematic 35mm photographic, intimate top-down angle.

des_07_blueprint.brief: Warm, intimate top-down shot of an architectural blueprint with nested rectangles. Evokes 'the show is a file-system' without labels. Sits as the last visual before the references, pairing with the final paragraph's reframing of the special as a map.
des_07_blueprint.rationale: A still image on the closing beat gives the piece a visual rest; adding another interactive here would overload the reader just before the end.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial — warm amber accents on near-black background, feels like a late-night read after the show
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: text-first within each section; each section ends with its visual (chart, callout, or interactive). Section 1 is the exception — the animated arc appears before the text so the reader sees the 46-minute gap first.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Body text Georgia 18px, labels and UI in system-ui. Stat callouts 72px serif numerals with system-ui descriptors below. Pull quotes (Wong's spoken lines) in italic serif with an amber vertical rule on the left. Section dividers as thin 1px warm amber rules.
